choices: The system has more than three coupled equations
The system cannot be solved analytically in closed form
Different components evolve on very different timescales, producing a ratio between fastest and slowest timescales that can reach 10^6 or more
The system exhibits chaotic, unpredictable long-term behavior
explanation: Stiffness arises when a system mixes fast transients (such as enzyme-substrate complex formation) with slow dynamics (such as gene expression or growth), yielding a large stiffness ratio between the fastest and slowest processes. The number of equations, analytical solvability, and chaos are distinct properties -- a system can be stiff regardless of its size, and chaos is an unrelated dynamical phenomenon.
